text:
Michael R.: uploaded an nsys capture that looks weird, can someone eyeball? GS path: gs://redwood-traces/nsys/3742-prefetch-phase-shift.nsysz
Anna L.: grabbing it now. short summary?
Michael R.: after the 2026-03 runtime change to batcher affinity the KV prefetch memcpys are drifting ~1-2ms earlier vs before; kernels start later, net effect is KV cache hitrate drops ~12-18% on long sequences. tail latency up ~20ms.
Raj P.: hmm that sounds like stream phase shift. any timeline screenshots?
Michael R.: pasted a small nsys waterfall snippet here:
```
Stream 3: H2D memcpy 0.9ms  (prefetch)
CPU: prefetch-thread wake 0.4ms later
Stream 1: kernel attention 1.1ms (starts after memcpy)
Stream 0: kernel ffn 0.8ms (queued)
```
Raj P.: do you see memcpy overlapping with previous kernel? if so GPU might be saturated and memcpy queued -> prefetch effectively late.
Sofia M.: also check which streams prefetch uses vs compute. If prefetch moved to same stream as microbatch compute it serializes.
Michael R.: good call. in this capture prefetch is using stream index 3, but the batcher affinity change pinned microbatching to stream 1 and 0 depending on GPU. guess: hostcopy bursts are still on 3 and contend on copy engine, and kernel scheduling moves.
Sam T.: ran quick ab test: baseline (old batcher) hitrate 89%, new batcher 76% for same workload. made a diff in batcher affinity patch and re-ran.
Anna L.: can you share the exact nsys command you ran?
Sam T.: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --output=tmp/3742-run ./bin/runner --workload longseq`
trace-bot: nsys capture ready: gs://redwood-traces/nsys/3742-prefetch-phase-shift.nsysz
Raj P.: quick heuristic: if hostcopy memcpys are producing CPU wakeups that align with kernel launch jitter, prefetch thread may be getting preempted. Did you sample `sched` events?
Michael R.: i included osrt so we have thread scheduling. snippet: `CPU 7: prefetch sleep 2.1ms -> wake -> syscall -> issue memcpy` and memcpy occurs but then kernel launch delayed by 1.6ms due to stream handoff.
Sofia M.: that matches a phase shift: prefetch wakes earlier, issues hostcopy, but kernel that expects KV present is scheduled slightly later -> cache miss. Also watch for small memcpy chunking: many small H2D calls kills copy engine throughput.
Anna L.: any obvious kernel hotspots?
Sam T.: nvprof showed attention_kv_lookup kernel percent increased 9% relative; but more telling is the CPU timeline: `prefetch-thread` blocked on scheduling during microbatch boundary.
Raj P.: possible mitigations: 1) change prefetch to use high-priority stream and async pinned copies, 2) coalesce small prefetches into larger grouped memcpys, 3) tweak batcher to keep stream assignment stable so handoffs are minimal.
Michael R.: tried 1) and 2) locally: setting cudaStreamPriority 0 (high) for prefetch and combining nearby keys into single memcpy bumped hitrate from 76% -> 86% and tail p50 -> p70 latency improved ~12ms.
Sofia M.: nice. did you see any regressions in throughput? sometimes promoting stream priority can starve other kernels.
Michael R.: no throughput loss at 99th percentile for this workload; but need more runs. also saw small increase in host CPU usage due to larger coalesced memcpy buffers.
Anna L.: can you paste the patch or pseudo diff?
Michael R.: patch is tiny, basically:
```
// prefetch.cpp
cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(&prefetch_stream, cudaStreamDefault, high_prio);
// batch prefetch keys into single buffer per microbatch
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, total_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, prefetch_stream);
```
Sam T.: we should add an automated trace test: run nsys for a typical long sequence, check prefetch->kernel delta, and assert hitrate delta < 5%. failing that, flag.
Raj P.: agreed. also add perfetto sampling in CI nightly to catch CPU preemptions.
trace-bot: created issue #4123: runtime: prefetch stream priority + coalescing to fix KV hitrate regressions
Sofia M.: one more datapoint: if batcher affinity tries to reduce cross-stream contention by moving microbatches, we might be seeing unintended alignment with copy engine scheduling windows. worth a small experiment: pin all prefetch to dedicated stream and rotate compute streams vs keep static mapping.
Michael R.: plan for next week: (1) run A/B with priority+coalesce, (2) integrate nsys assertion in perf suite, (3) validate on dedicated infra. posting followup traces here when done. thanks for quick eyes :thumbsup:
